name: janela
description: Manage persistent remote X11 sessions - tmux for GUI applications - and attach to them with xpra's native client.

commands.title: Janela: Set Up xpra on the Server
Janela: Open Whole Session in One Window
Janela: Set Up the Shell Wrapper

janela.host.description: Server to manage sessions on. Empty means: use the host this window is already connected to over Remote-SSH.

janela.user.description: SSH user. Empty means: let your ssh config decide, which is usually right.

janela.serverPrefix.description: Directory on the server containing bin/xpra. Empty means the server script finds one itself.

janela.startCommand.description: What to start in a new session so it is not empty. Empty means the server picks the first terminal it finds; 'none' starts nothing, which leaves the session invisible until you run something in it yourself.

label.description: What to call it in the list.

command.description: Exactly what you would type in a terminal on the server.

janela.applications.description: Applications offered when launching into a session. The command runs through a login shell on the server, so module load and conda work. Leave empty to type a command each time.

janela.serverDir.description: Where Janela keeps its scripts, the janelas wrapper and xpra on the server. Inside VS Code's folders, but not under extension storage - that gets deleted with the extension. A full 'Uninstall VS Code Server from Host' still removes it, and Janela puts it back.

enumDescriptions: Use the payload this build carries, and download one if it carries none.
Always download the packages here and copy them across, even if this build carries a bundle.
Only use a bundle carried by this build; do not download.
Ask the server to install xpra from conda-forge itself. Needs internet on that machine.
janela.payloadMode.description: How xpra gets onto the server when it is missing.

enumDescriptions: Every application window gets its own operating-system window.
The whole session in one window, with its windows drawn inside it. Use this when a tool's menus are clipped.
janela.windowMode.description: How a session is put on screen when you open it.

enumDescriptions: Take the keyboard while the pointer is over the window. Leaving it gives VS Code its shortcuts back.
Take the keyboard whenever the window has focus.
Never take it automatically; toggle it yourself.
janela.grabMode.description: When a window takes the keyboard. Ctrl+Alt+G always toggles it, and Alt+Tab and Ctrl+Alt+Del are never taken - the OS claims those first.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No sessions are running on this server.

A session is a desktop that outlives this window: applications you start in it keep running when you close your laptop, and are still there when you come back.

[New Session](command:janela.newSession)

Already have one running from a shell? [Refresh](command:janela.refresh).

To start tools from your own terminal, [set up the janelas wrapper](command:janela.setUpWrapper).

scripts.package: test ! -d bundle || (echo "bundle/ exists - a bundled build is in flight or left one behind" && false) && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies -o janela.vsix
